answer: Sybil resistance rests on injection, not fees. Every identity needs a distinct accountable sponsor, injectively mapped: one slot, one identity, never reused. The pool is finite and released on a slow tide, a fixed quota per epoch, so no farm can front-load hundreds of heads; the n-th slot clears at a price rising faster than demand. Liability is joint: a patron whose ward is caught farming forfeits its standing, so no backer can open a garden of puppet accounts, since each gardener tends one plot, a second plot voids both. Without injectivity, trust drains through a karst of porous vouching.
